probe: What are we measuring when it seems everyone else has "figured it out"?
premise: Other people's external milestones mean they have achieved internal certainty.

pairs.reflection: idk honestly. like job titles i guess? people from uni are on linkedin saying theyre "excited to announce" stuff and im just like.. still here. not sure what else there is to measure
pairs.reply: Let's go slowly. When someone announces a new job title, what does that actually tell us about what it feels like to be them?

pairs.reflection: idk. nothing really? i guess it doesnt tell me how they feel, just that they got the job. but it always looks like they know what theyre doing and im just.. not there
pairs.reply: When it looks like they know what they are doing, is that something visible in them, or something we fill in from where we stand?

pairs.reflection: idk probably filling it in? like i know its just a post. but i still look at it and think they must know what theyre doing, otherwise why would they be there. maybe thats just me tho
pairs.reply: If getting a job required someone to first know what they were doing with their life, how many of those posts would actually exist?

pairs.reflection: idk fewer maybe? i mean i get what youre saying. probably lots of them are just winging it too. but it doesnt really feel like that when im scrolling at 11pm lol
pairs.reply: In that moment scrolling at 11pm, what makes their announcement feel like proof of something solid inside them?

pairs.reflection: idk i think its the photo and the title and everyone commenting congrats. it just looks finished? like theyve arrived somewhere and im still in my bed on my phone
pairs.reply: "Finished." When you see that finished picture, are you seeing certainty in their life, or the contrast with where you're sitting?

pairs.reflection: the contrast probably. like theyre just a photo and im actually here in my room so of course i feel worse. idk its not really about them i guess
pairs.reply: If it isn't really about them, what is the finished picture an image of?

pairs.reflection: idk. like what i think i should have by now maybe? i dont really know what that is tho. just something that looks sorted i guess
pairs.reply: "Something that looks sorted." When you imagine yourself feeling sorted, what is actually different on the inside?

pairs.reflection: idk. i guess i wouldnt be checking? like i wouldnt feel that dip when i see a post. just calmer maybe. not sure what else
pairs.reply: If the calm is about not needing to check, does "figuring it out" live in what we achieve, or in stopping the comparison?

pairs.reflection: idk maybe the second one? but its hard to stop checking when i do feel behind. like if i actually had a thing id stop probably. not sure those are separate tbh
pairs.reply: When you imagine having "a thing," is it to live that life, or to have proof against the feeling of being behind?

pairs.reflection: idk both? i think proof mostly if im being honest. but then i dont even know what the thing would be so its a bit pointless lol
pairs.reply: If the thing is mostly wanted as proof against falling behind, what would it actually take to feel like you've caught up?

pairs.reflection: idk. i dont think i know what caught up even looks like. like no one ever says "ok youre level now". i guess just not feeling like everyone else is ahead? but that probably wouldnt ever happen lol
pairs.reply: If there is no finish line where someone says you are level, what are you actually measuring yourself against?

event.openQuestion: If there is no finish line where someone says you are level, what are you actually measuring yourself against?
